questions.text: Complete the statement: "Fisheries can be defined as" by choosing the correct option.
options: The catching, processing and marketing of fish
questions.explanation: Fisheries encompass all activities related to catching, processing and marketing of fish.

questions.text: Which branch of fisheries involves raising fish in controlled environments?
questions.explanation: Aquaculture is the branch of fisheries dealing with raising fish in controlled environments.

questions.text: Which of the following is a freshwater fish?
questions.explanation: Tilapia is a commonly cultured freshwater fish species.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "The bony fish belong to the class" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Osteichthyes is the class of bony fishes.

questions.text: Which of the following is a cartilaginous fish?
questions.explanation: Sharks are cartilaginous fish (class Chondrichthyes).

questions.text: The lateral line system in fish is used for
options: Detecting vibrations and pressure changes in water
questions.explanation: The lateral line detects vibrations and pressure changes in the surrounding water.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Gills in fish function primarily to" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Gills are respiratory organs that extract dissolved oxygen from water.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "The swim bladder helps fish to" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: The swim bladder is a gas-filled organ that helps fish regulate buoyancy.

questions.text: Which type of scales is found on a typical bony fish?
questions.explanation: Most bony fish have cycloid or ctenoid scales.

questions.text: Which fin is responsible for propulsion in most fish?
questions.explanation: The caudal (tail) fin provides the main thrust for forward movement.

questions.text: A brackish water environment is one where
options: Fresh water mixes with salt water
questions.explanation: Brackish water occurs where rivers meet the sea, mixing fresh and salt water.

questions.text: Which of the following is an estuarine fish species?
questions.explanation: Mudskippers thrive in estuarine and brackish water environments.

questions.text: Marine fish live in water with salinity above
questions.explanation: Marine waters typically have salinity above 30 parts per thousand.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Anadromous fish are those that" by choosing the correct option.
options: Migrate from freshwater to sea to spawn
questions.explanation: Anadromous fish like salmon migrate from freshwater to the ocean and back to freshwater to spawn.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Catadromous fish migrate to" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Catadromous fish like eels live in freshwater but migrate to the sea to spawn.

questions.text: The most common fish pond shape in tropical aquaculture is
questions.explanation: Rectangular ponds are the most common due to ease of construction and management.

questions.text: The inlet of a fish pond should be located
options: At the shallowest end, opposite the drain
At the centre of the pond
questions.explanation: The inlet should be at the shallow end and the outlet at the deep end for good water circulation.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Pond liming is done primarily to" by choosing the correct option.
options: Raise the pH and reduce acidity
questions.explanation: Liming raises pond pH, reduces acidity and helps control parasites.

questions.text: The standard depth of a fish production pond is between
questions.explanation: Production ponds are typically 1.0 to 1.5 metres deep for effective management.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a type of aquaculture system?
questions.explanation: Trawling is a capture method, not an aquaculture system.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Cage culture is best suited for" by choosing the correct option.
options: Large water bodies like lakes and rivers
questions.explanation: Cage culture uses net enclosures in existing large water bodies.

questions.text: Pen culture differs from cage culture in that pens
options: Are enclosed by barriers fixed to the bottom
questions.explanation: Pens are enclosures where the bottom is sealed by the natural pond or lake bed.

questions.text: Recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) are used to
questions.explanation: RAS filters and recycles water, allowing intensive fish culture in limited water.

questions.text: The ideal pH range for most freshwater fish ponds is
questions.explanation: Most freshwater fish thrive in a pH range of 6.5 to 8.5.

questions.text: Dissolved oxygen in water is essential for fish because it
questions.explanation: Fish extract dissolved oxygen through their gills for cellular respiration.

questions.text: High turbidity in a fish pond is caused by
options: Excessive suspended particles such as soil and algae
questions.explanation: Turbidity results from suspended sediments, soil erosion or algal blooms.

questions.text: The ideal water temperature range for tilapia culture is
questions.explanation: Tilapia perform optimally between 25 and 30 degrees Celsius.

questions.text: Which of the following is a measure of water salinity?
questions.explanation: Salinity is measured using a salinometer or by electrical conductivity.

questions.text: Ammonia build-up in fish ponds is dangerous because it
options: Is toxic to fish and can cause gill damage
questions.explanation: Ammonia from fish waste is highly toxic and can damage gill tissues.

questions.text: Water hardness is primarily a measure of
questions.explanation: Water hardness is determined by dissolved calcium and magnesium ions.

questions.text: Which of the following is an omnivorous fish?
questions.explanation: Tilapia feeds on both plant and animal matter, making it omnivorous.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Carnivorous fish primarily feed on" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Carnivorous fish feed mainly on other fish, insects and aquatic animals.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Herbivorous fish feed mainly on" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Herbivorous fish feed primarily on algae and plant material.

questions.text: Floating feed is preferred in cage culture because it
questions.explanation: Floating feed stays on the surface, allowing farmers to observe feeding behaviour.

questions.text: The protein requirement of fish fry is generally
options: The same as that of adults
questions.explanation: Young fish have higher protein requirements for rapid growth and development.

questions.text: Feed conversion ratio (FCR) measures the
options: Amount of feed needed to produce a unit weight of fish
Number of feeding times per day
questions.explanation: FCR is the ratio of feed given to the weight gain of the fish.

questions.text: A lower feed conversion ratio indicates
questions.explanation: A lower FCR means less feed is required to produce a unit of fish weight.

questions.text: Which of the following is a plant-based protein source in fish feeds?
questions.explanation: Soybean meal is a common plant-based protein ingredient in fish feeds.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Feeding fish too much leads to" by choosing the correct option.
options: Water pollution and poor water quality
questions.explanation: Overfeeding causes excess waste, decomposition and deteriorating water quality.

questions.text: The feeding frequency for fingerlings is generally
options: Two to three times a day
questions.explanation: Young fish have smaller stomachs and benefit from frequent small feedings.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Most fish reproduce by" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Most fish species are oviparous, reproducing by laying eggs.

questions.text: A fish hatchery is a facility used to
options: Incubate eggs and rear young fish
questions.explanation: Hatcheries are specialised facilities for incubating eggs and rearing fry and fingerlings.

questions.text: In catfish culture, induced breeding is often necessary because
options: Natural spawning conditions may not occur in captivity
questions.explanation: Captive catfish may not receive the natural environmental cues needed for spawning.

questions.text: Which hormone is commonly used for induced breeding of fish?
questions.explanation: HCG is widely used to induce ovulation in captive fish species.

questions.text: The process of stripping fish involves
options: Manually expressing eggs or milt from the gonads
questions.explanation: Stripping is the manual collection of eggs or sperm from brood fish.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Fry are best described as" by choosing the correct option.
options: Recently hatched fish that still carry yolk sac
questions.explanation: Fry are newly hatched fish, often still absorbing their yolk sac.

questions.text: Fingerlings are young fish that have
options: Absorbed their yolk sac and are feeding externally
Been in the ocean for years
questions.explanation: Fingerlings are post-larval fish that feed on external food sources.

questions.text: External fertilisation in fish means
options: Eggs are fertilised inside the female
Eggs and sperm meet outside the body in water
questions.explanation: In external fertilisation, eggs and sperm are released into the water where fertilisation occurs.

questions.text: What does the term Broodstock in aquaculture refer to in animal husbandry?
options: Mature fish kept for breeding purposes
questions.explanation: Broodstock are selected mature fish used as breeding parents in hatcheries.

questions.text: What does the term "In tilapia, mouth brooding" mean?
options: The female builds a nest for eggs
The female incubates eggs in her mouth
Eggs are left unprotected on rocks
questions.explanation: Female tilapia hold fertilised eggs in their mouths for incubation and protection.

questions.text: The most important fish disease in tropical aquaculture is caused by
questions.explanation: Bacterial infections, especially Aeromonas species, are major disease threats in warm-water fish culture.

questions.text: White spot disease in fish is caused by
questions.explanation: White spot or ich is caused by the protozoan parasite Ichthyophthirius multifiliis.

questions.text: Fungal infections in fish ponds are common when
options: Fish are injured and water quality is poor
questions.explanation: Fungi like Saprolegnia infect wounds on fish, especially when conditions are stressful.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Fish lice (Argulus) are" by choosing the correct option.
options: Ectoparasites that attach to the body surface
questions.explanation: Argulus is an external parasite that attaches to fish skin and feeds on blood.

questions.text: The swim bladder disease (furunculosis) primarily affects
questions.explanation: Furunculosis is a bacterial disease that causes abscesses in the swim bladder and kidneys.

questions.text: The main route of disease transmission in fish ponds is through
questions.explanation: Waterborne pathogens spread rapidly through shared water in ponds.

questions.text: Routine disinfection of fish ponds between culture cycles is important to
options: Break disease cycles and reduce pathogen load
questions.explanation: Disinfection between cycles removes pathogens and reduces the risk of disease outbreaks.

questions.text: A common sign of bacterial infection in fish is
questions.explanation: Bacterial infections often present as skin lesions, haemorrhages and fin erosion.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Diplopstomum is a type of" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Diplopstomum is a trematode (fluke) that commonly infects fish eyes and skin.

questions.text: The best preventive measure against fish disease is
options: Maintaining good water quality and proper nutrition
questions.explanation: Good water quality and nutrition strengthen fish immunity and prevent disease.

questions.text: Which of the following is a predator of juvenile fish in ponds?
options: Birds such as kingfishers and herons
questions.explanation: Wading birds are major predators of fish in open ponds.

questions.text: Cormorants and kingfishers are a major threat to
options: Fingerlings and juvenile fish in ponds
questions.explanation: These birds prey heavily on small fish in ponds and cages.

questions.text: Catfish fingerlings can be protected from bird predation by
options: Using netting or covers over ponds
questions.explanation: Overhead netting prevents predatory birds from reaching the fish.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Snakes may prey on fish in ponds by" by choosing the correct option.
options: Entering ponds from the banks to catch fish
questions.explanation: Snakes access ponds from the banks and feed on fish near the surface.

questions.text: Cannibalism is a significant problem in catfish culture when
options: There is a large size difference among fish in the same tank
questions.explanation: Size-grading is essential because larger catfish will eat smaller ones.

questions.text: Smoking fish is a preservation method that
options: Dries and flavours fish using smoke heat
questions.explanation: Smoking combines heat and smoke compounds to preserve and flavour fish.

questions.text: Sun-drying fish is most effective in areas with
questions.explanation: Sun-drying requires hot, dry conditions with good air circulation.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Salting fish preserves them by" by choosing the correct option.
options: Drawing out moisture and creating an unfavourable environment for bacteria
questions.explanation: Salt draws out moisture through osmosis, inhibiting bacterial growth.

questions.text: Freezing is one of the best methods of fish preservation because it
options: Slows down microbial and enzymatic activity
questions.explanation: Low temperatures slow microbial growth and enzyme activity, keeping fish fresh longer.

questions.text: What does Canning fish involve in the context of fishing?
options: Sealing fish in airtight containers and heat-processing them
questions.explanation: Canning seals fish in containers and uses heat to kill bacteria and create a vacuum.

questions.text: Icing fish immediately after catch is important to
options: Increase the weight of the fish
Slow down spoilage by reducing temperature
Change the colour of the fish
questions.explanation: Rapid chilling slows bacterial growth and enzymatic degradation.

questions.text: Fermentation in fish processing is used to produce
options: Condiments such as fish sauce and fermented fish paste
questions.explanation: Controlled fermentation produces traditional products like fish sauce and bagoong.

questions.text: A gill net is designed to catch fish by
options: Filtering fish through mesh that holds them by the gills
questions.explanation: In a gill net, fish swim in through the mesh but are held by their gill covers.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "A cast net is mainly used to catch" by choosing the correct option.
options: Small schooling fish in shallow water
questions.explanation: Cast nets are hand-thrown circular nets used to catch small fish in shallow waters.

questions.text: What does Trawling involve in the context of fishing?
options: Dragging a large net through water behind a boat
questions.explanation: Trawling pulls a cone-shaped net along the bottom or through the water column.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Long-line fishing uses" by choosing the correct option.
options: A main line with many baited hooks attached at intervals
questions.explanation: Long lines have hundreds or thousands of baited hooks along a main line.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Seine nets are used to" by choosing the correct option.
options: Encircle and enclose schools of fish in shallow water
questions.explanation: Seine nets are drawn around a school of fish to enclose and capture them.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Fish pots or traps are" by choosing the correct option.
options: Enclosed structures that allow fish to enter but make exit difficult
questions.explanation: Fish traps use funnel-like entrances that let fish in but prevent easy escape.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Using dynamite to catch fish is" by choosing the correct option.
options: Illegal and destructive to the aquatic environment
questions.explanation: Blast fishing destroys habitats, kills non-target species and is banned in most countries.

questions.text: What does the term By-catch in fishing refer to in animal husbandry?
options: Unwanted species caught alongside the target fish
Fish released back into the sea alive
questions.explanation: By-catch includes non-target species accidentally captured during fishing operations.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Overfishing occurs when" by choosing the correct option.
options: Fish are caught at a rate slower than they reproduce
Fish are caught faster than they can reproduce and replenish
questions.explanation: Overfishing depletes fish stocks beyond their ability to recover naturally.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Maximum sustainable yield (MSY) is" by choosing the correct option.
options: The maximum amount of fish that can be caught forever
The largest catch that can be taken indefinitely without depleting the stock
The maximum number of ponds a farm can have
The highest price fish can be sold for
questions.explanation: MSY is the optimal harvest level that maintains the fish population over time.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "A fishing licence is required to" by choosing the correct option.
options: Legally engage in commercial or recreational fishing
questions.explanation: Licensing helps regulate fishing effort and protect fish stocks.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Fish sanctuaries are areas where" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Sanctuaries are no-fishing zones established to allow fish stocks to recover.

questions.text: Closed season in fisheries refers to
options: A period when fish markets are closed
A period when fishing is prohibited to allow breeding and spawning
questions.explanation: Closed seasons protect fish during critical breeding periods.

questions.text: The most commonly cultured catfish species in West Africa is
questions.explanation: Clarias gariepinus (African catfish) is the dominant aquaculture catfish species in West Africa.

questions.text: Oreochromis niloticus is commonly known as
questions.explanation: Oreochromis niloticus is the Nile tilapia, widely cultured in tropical regions.

questions.text: Which of the following is an advantage of tilapia culture?
options: It is hardy, fast-growing and omnivorous
It cannot tolerate poor water quality
questions.explanation: Tilapia are adaptable, fast-growing and can feed on a wide range of foods.

questions.text: The common carp (Cyprinus carpio) belongs to the family
questions.explanation: The common carp belongs to the family Cyprinidae.

questions.text: Heterobranchus bidorsalis is a species of
questions.explanation: Heterobranchus bidorsalis is an air-breathing catfish cultured in West Africa.

questions.text: Clarias gariepinus can survive in low-oxygen water because it
options: Possesses a labyrinth organ for air breathing
Stores oxygen in its swim bladder
questions.explanation: Catfish have accessory air-breathing organs that allow them to gulp atmospheric air.

questions.text: Pacu (Colossoma macropomum) is mainly cultured for
options: Its high-quality flesh for human consumption
questions.explanation: Pacu is a large freshwater fish valued for its meat in aquaculture.

questions.text: Which of the following is an ornamental fish species?
questions.explanation: Betta splendens is widely kept as an ornamental fish for its vivid colours.

questions.text: AQUAPONICS combines aquaculture with
questions.explanation: Aquaponics integrates fish culture with soilless plant growing in a symbiotic system.

questions.text: In aquaponics, the nutrient-rich water for plants comes from
questions.explanation: Fish excrete ammonia and nutrients that are converted by bacteria into plant-available forms.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "A major advantage of aquaponics is" by choosing the correct option.
options: It reduces water waste and produces both fish and vegetables
It eliminates the need for fish feed
It works only in cold climates
questions.explanation: Aquaponics reuses water between fish and plants, reducing overall water consumption.

questions.text: The role of nitrifying bacteria in aquaponics is to
options: Convert ammonia to nitrite and then to nitrate for plant uptake
questions.explanation: Nitrosomonas converts ammonia to nitrite, and Nitrobacter converts nitrite to nitrate.

questions.text: Tilapia is the most preferred fish species in aquaponics because it
options: Tolerates a wide range of conditions and feeds on plant-based diets
questions.explanation: Tilapia are hardy, adaptable and can thrive on the high-protein feeds used in aquaponics.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Pond fertilisation is done to" by choosing the correct option.
options: Stimulate natural food organisms such as plankton growth
questions.explanation: Fertilisers promote plankton growth, which serves as natural food for fish.

questions.text: Organic fertilisers used in fish ponds include
questions.explanation: Animal manure and compost are common organic fertilisers that promote plankton growth.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Stocking density refers to the" by choosing the correct option.
options: Number of fish per unit area or volume of water
Total weight of feed given per day
Number of ponds on a farm
questions.explanation: Stocking density is the number of fish stocked per unit area or volume.

questions.text: High stocking density in fish ponds can lead to
options: Stress, disease, poor water quality and cannibalism
questions.explanation: Overcrowding causes stress, degrades water quality and increases disease risk.

questions.text: Culled or graded fish are separated to
options: Reduce cannibalism and ensure uniform growth
questions.explanation: Grading separates fish by size to prevent cannibalism and promote even growth.

questions.text: The water exchange rate in a fish pond should be
options: Sufficient to maintain good water quality
questions.explanation: Regular water exchange removes waste products and replenishes dissolved oxygen.

questions.text: Earthen ponds are preferred in aquaculture because they
options: Allow natural food production and are cost-effective
questions.explanation: Earthen ponds support natural food webs and are cheaper than concrete tanks.

questions.text: Concrete tanks are used in aquaculture mainly because they
options: Allow better control of water and hygiene
questions.explanation: Concrete tanks are easy to clean, disinfect and manage compared to earthen ponds.

questions.text: A water inlet pipe in a fish pond should be
options: Placed at the bottom of the drain
Positioned above water level to allow splashing and aeration
questions.explanation: Positioning the inlet above the water surface helps aerate incoming water.

questions.text: The monsoon season in West Africa often causes
options: Flooding, pond overflow and mixing of wild and cultured fish
Lower water temperatures in marine farms
questions.explanation: Heavy rains cause flooding that can breach ponds and introduce wild fish and diseases.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Pond dykes serve the purpose of" by choosing the correct option.
options: Containing the water and providing access around the pond
questions.explanation: Dykes are embankments that hold water and provide walkways for management activities.

questions.text: Siltation in fish ponds reduces their
questions.explanation: Silt accumulates on the pond bottom, reducing depth and available water volume.

questions.text: The walkway around a fish pond is called a
questions.explanation: The bund or dyke is the raised embankment surrounding the pond.

questions.text: A settling basin at the inlet of a fish pond is used to
options: Remove sediment and debris before water enters the pond
questions.explanation: Settling basins allow suspended particles to settle before water enters the culture pond.

questions.text: Dissolved oxygen levels in fish ponds are lowest at
options: Midday when the sun is strongest
questions.explanation: Oxygen levels drop overnight as respiration continues without photosynthesis.

questions.text: Algal blooms in fish ponds can be dangerous because they
options: Cause oxygen depletion when the bloom crashes
questions.explanation: When algal blooms die and decompose, they consume large amounts of dissolved oxygen.

questions.text: An aerator in a fish pond is used to
questions.explanation: Aerators mechanically increase oxygen levels in pond water.

questions.text: The term fry refers to fish that are
questions.explanation: Fry are the earliest free-swimming stage of fish after hatching.

questions.text: What does the term Spawn in fish culture refer to in animal husbandry?
questions.explanation: Spawn are the eggs and newly hatched larvae of fish.

questions.text: Sex reversal in tilapia fingerlings is done using
questions.explanation: MT is fed to tilapia fry during the early growth stage to produce all-male populations.

questions.text: All-male tilapia populations are preferred because male tilapia
options: Grow faster and avoid uncontrolled reproduction
questions.explanation: Male tilapia grow approximately 40-60% faster than females and prevent overcrowding from spawning.

questions.text: Artificial fertilisation in fish involves
options: Manually mixing eggs and sperm outside the body
questions.explanation: Artificial fertilisation is the controlled mixing of stripped eggs and milt.

questions.text: What does the term Spermiation in male fish refer to in animal husbandry?
questions.explanation: Spermiation is the release of milt (sperm) from the male gonads.

questions.text: Egg incubation in hatcheries requires
options: Clean, well-aerated water at the correct temperature
questions.explanation: Incubating eggs need dissolved oxygen, clean water and optimal temperatures.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Egg sac fry are at risk of" by choosing the correct option.
options: Suffocation if water flow is inadequate
questions.explanation: Egg sac fry are immobile and need well-aerated water flowing over them.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Nursery ponds are used to" by choosing the correct option.
options: Rear fry and fingerlings to a suitable size for grow-out
questions.explanation: Nursery ponds provide a protected environment for the early growth stages.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Fish transport is best done with" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Fish need sufficient dissolved oxygen and cool temperatures during transport to reduce stress.

questions.text: Transporting fish in plastic bags with oxygen is a method called
options: Live fish transport in sealed polythene bags
questions.explanation: Fish are sealed in polythene bags with water and pure oxygen for short-distance transport.

questions.text: A sedative like MS-222 is sometimes used during fish transport to
questions.explanation: Sedatives calm fish, lower oxygen consumption and reduce transport stress.

questions.text: The culture period for catfish from stocking to harvest in West Africa is approximately
questions.explanation: African catfish typically reach market size in 5 to 8 months under good conditions.

questions.text: Harvesting fish from a pond is usually done by
options: Waiting for them to jump out
questions.explanation: Seine nets or complete draining are the most practical harvesting methods.

questions.text: What does Partial harvesting involve in the context of fishing?
options: Selectively removing the largest fish while leaving others to grow
questions.explanation: Partial harvesting allows smaller fish to continue growing for later sale.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Fish is a good source of" by choosing the correct option.
options: High-quality protein and essential fatty acids
questions.explanation: Fish provides high biological value protein and omega-3 fatty acids.

questions.text: Omega-3 fatty acids found in fish are beneficial for
questions.explanation: Omega-3 fatty acids reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease and support brain function.

questions.text: The food value chain in fisheries includes
questions.explanation: The value chain covers all stages from production through to the final consumer.

questions.text: Post-harvest losses in fisheries are mainly caused by
options: Poor handling, inadequate ice supply and lack of processing facilities
questions.explanation: Lack of ice, poor transport and minimal processing lead to high post-harvest losses.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Iridovirus disease in fish affects" by choosing the correct option.
options: The immune system and organs of fish, especially fingerlings
questions.explanation: Iridovirus causes high mortality in young fish, affecting immune function and organs.

questions.text: Aquatic plants in a fish pond benefit the culture by
options: Providing shelter, oxygen and supplementary food
questions.explanation: Aquatic plants produce oxygen, shelter juvenile fish and may serve as supplemental food.

questions.text: The swim bladder of a physoclistous fish is closed, meaning
options: Gas is secreted and absorbed through the blood, not the gut
It has a connection to the oesophagus
questions.explanation: Physoclistous fish have a closed swim bladder; gas exchange occurs via the gas gland.

questions.text: A physostomous fish has a swim bladder that
options: Has no connection to the digestive tract
Is connected to the oesophagus by a pneumatic duct
questions.explanation: Physostomous fish can gulp or release air through a duct connecting the swim bladder to the gut.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "The operculum in fish is the" by choosing the correct option.
options: Bony flap covering and protecting the gills
questions.explanation: The operculum is a hard bony cover that protects the delicate gill structures.

questions.text: Mucus on fish skin serves the function of
options: Protecting against parasites, bacteria and reducing friction
questions.explanation: The slime coat is a primary defence against pathogens and aids hydrodynamics.

questions.text: The pyloric caeca in fish are finger-like projections that
options: Increase the surface area for digestion and absorption
questions.explanation: Pyloric caeca are digestive organs that increase the absorptive area of the intestine.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Fish kidneys mainly function to" by choosing the correct option.
options: Regulate water balance and excrete nitrogenous waste
questions.explanation: The kidney maintains osmoregulation and removes metabolic waste from the blood.

questions.text: Osmoregulation in freshwater fish involves
options: Producing large volumes of dilute urine to counteract water gain
questions.explanation: Freshwater fish gain water by osmosis and must excrete excess water as dilute urine.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Marine fish drink seawater to" by choosing the correct option.
options: Replace water lost by osmosis and absorb salts
questions.explanation: Marine fish lose water to their hypertonic environment and drink to compensate.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "The heart of a typical fish has" by choosing the correct option.
options: Two main chambers: one atrium and one ventricle
questions.explanation: The fish heart is a two-chambered pump (one atrium and one ventricle) in a single circuit.

questions.text: In a fish circulatory system, blood flows in a
options: Double circuit with separate pulmonary flow
Single circuit from heart to gills to body and back
questions.explanation: Fish have a single-loop circulatory system: heart to gills to body to heart.

questions.text: The Weberian apparatus found in some fish connects the
options: Swim bladder to the inner ear to enhance hearing
questions.explanation: The Weberian apparatus amplifies sound vibrations from the swim bladder to the inner ear.

questions.text: Ctenoid scales have comb-like edges and are found on
questions.explanation: Ctenoid scales with their tooth-like posterior margin are common in teleost fish.

questions.text: Placoid scales, also known as dermal denticles, are characteristic of
questions.explanation: Placoid scales give sharkskin its sandpaper-like texture and are homologous to teeth.

questions.text: The adipose fin is a small fleshy fin found between the dorsal and caudal fins in
options: Catfish, salmon and some other species
questions.explanation: The adipose fin is a characteristic feature of catfish, salmon and trout.

questions.text: Barbels on catfish are used primarily for
options: Sensing food and navigating in murky water
questions.explanation: Barbels are sensory organs rich in taste buds that help catfish find food in turbid water.

questions.text: The caudal fin shape that provides the most sustained swimming speed is
questions.explanation: Lunate (crescent-shaped) tails are hydrodynamically efficient for sustained fast swimming.

questions.text: The pectoral fins in fish are mainly used for
questions.explanation: Pectoral fins allow precise manoeuvring, stopping and hovering.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "The dorsal fin helps fish to" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: The dorsal fin acts as a keel to keep the fish upright and stable.

questions.text: The lateral line consists of a series of
options: Neuromasts or sensory cells along a canal system
questions.explanation: Neuromasts within the lateral line canal detect water displacement and vibrations.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Ichthyology is the study of" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Ichthyology is the branch of zoology devoted to the study of fish.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Limnology is the study of" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Limnology focuses on the physical, chemical and biological features of freshwater systems.

questions.text: The pelagic zone of the ocean refers to
options: The open water column away from the shore and bottom
questions.explanation: The pelagic zone is the open water area of the ocean, not the seabed.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Benthic fish are those that" by choosing the correct option.
options: Live on or near the bottom of a water body
questions.explanation: Benthic fish such as flatfish live on or close to the substrate.

questions.text: The photic zone in a water body is where
questions.explanation: The photic zone receives enough sunlight for photosynthesis by algae and plants.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Anoxic conditions in a pond mean" by choosing the correct option.
questions.explanation: Anoxic water has no dissolved oxygen and is lethal to most fish.

questions.text: Biological oxygen demand (BOD) in water indicates
options: The amount of salt in the water
The amount of oxygen needed by organisms to decompose organic matter
questions.explanation: High BOD indicates high organic pollution and potential oxygen depletion.

questions.text: Eutrophication of a water body results from
options: Excessive nutrient enrichment leading to algal blooms
questions.explanation: Excess nutrients from fertilisers or sewage cause rapid algal growth and oxygen depletion.

questions.text: The thermocline in a lake is the layer where
questions.explanation: The thermocline is the transitional layer between warm surface water and cold deep water.

questions.text: A seine net differs from a gill net because it
options: Encloses fish by surrounding them rather than entangling by gills
Is only used in the deep sea
questions.explanation: Seine nets are drawn around fish to enclose them; gill nets entangle fish in the mesh.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "A lift net is operated by" by choosing the correct option.
options: Lowering it into water, baiting fish, then lifting it up
questions.explanation: Lift nets are submerged, left for fish to congregate, then raised to capture them.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "A fyke net is a type of" by choosing the correct option.
options: Hoop net or trap used to catch fish in rivers and estuaries
questions.explanation: Fyke nets are cylindrical trap nets with funnel-shaped openings used in rivers.

questions.text: The escape gap in a fish trap allows
options: Undersized fish to exit while retaining marketable sizes
questions.explanation: Escape gaps help reduce by-catch of juvenile fish and promote sustainable harvesting.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Purse seine nets are used to catch" by choosing the correct option.
options: Large schools of pelagic fish like sardines and tuna
questions.explanation: Purse seines encircle schools of fish and then cinch closed at the bottom like a drawstring.

questions.text: What does Electrofishing involve in the context of fishing?
options: Using electric current to stun fish for capture
questions.explanation: Electrofishing uses controlled electric fields to temporarily stun fish for sampling or harvest.

questions.text: Dynamite fishing causes damage to the marine environment by
options: Destroying coral reefs, killing non-target species and disrupting habitats
questions.explanation: Blast fishing obliterates reef structures and causes widespread ecosystem damage.

questions.text: Cyanide fishing is harmful because it
options: Stuns and kills fish and damages coral ecosystems
questions.explanation: Cyanide poisons fish and destroys the reef organisms they depend on.

questions.text: Discards in commercial fishing refers to
options: Fish and other marine organisms thrown back into the sea, often dead or dying
questions.explanation: Discards are the unwanted portion of the catch that is returned to the sea, usually with high mortality.

questions.text: The exclusive economic zone (EEZ) extends
options: Up to 200 nautical miles from the coastal baseline
questions.explanation: The EEZ grants coastal states sovereign rights over marine resources up to 200 nautical miles.

questions.text: Fish aggregation devices (FADs) work by
options: Repelling fish away from an area
Attracting pelagic fish to congregate around a floating structure
questions.explanation: FADs provide shade and shelter that attract schools of pelagic fish.

questions.text: Artisanal fishing is characterised by
options: Large factory vessels and advanced technology
questions.explanation: Artisanal fisheries use traditional methods and small boats, often for local consumption.

questions.text: A fish market is important in the fisheries sector because it
options: Provides a venue for price determination, distribution and sale of fish
questions.explanation: Fish markets are crucial nodes in the value chain for price setting and product distribution.

questions.text: Value addition in fisheries includes
options: Processing raw fish into smoked, dried or canned products for higher value
Releasing fish back into the sea
questions.explanation: Processing increases the shelf life and market value of fish products.

questions.text: A major challenge facing fisheries in West Africa is
questions.explanation: IUU fishing by both local and foreign vessels depletes West African fish stocks.

questions.text: Climate change affects fisheries primarily by
options: Altering water temperatures, sea levels and fish distribution patterns
questions.explanation: Changing temperatures shift fish habitats, affect breeding cycles and alter ecosystem productivity.

questions.text: The monofilament gill net is preferred over multifilament because it
options: Is less visible underwater, increasing catch efficiency
questions.explanation: Monofilament lines are nearly invisible in water, making fish less likely to detect them.

questions.text: A drag net or shrimp trawl typically has a
options: Cod end where the catch accumulates
questions.explanation: The cod end is the tapered rear section where captured shrimp and fish collect.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "The mesh size of a net determines" by choosing the correct option.
options: The minimum size of fish that can be retained
questions.explanation: Larger mesh allows smaller fish to escape, protecting juvenile stocks.

questions.text: A fish dryer or solar dryer improves upon sun drying by
options: Providing controlled airflow and protection from insects and dust
questions.explanation: Solar dryers use transparent covers to trap heat while keeping insects and debris out.

questions.text: Hot smoking cooks fish while cold smoking mainly
options: Preserves the fish without fully cooking it
questions.explanation: Cold smoking flavours and preserves fish at temperatures below 30 degrees Celsius.

questions.text: What does Filleting fish involve in the context of fishing?
options: Cutting the flesh away from the bones in clean portions
questions.explanation: Filleting removes the edible flesh from the bone structure for convenient cooking and sale.

questions.text: Vacuum packaging of fish products helps to
options: Add more water to the product
Exclude air and reduce oxidative spoilage
questions.explanation: Removing air slows aerobic bacterial growth and oxidative rancidity in fatty fish.

questions.text: Freeze-drying of fish is a preservation method that
options: Removes moisture under vacuum at low temperatures
questions.explanation: Freeze-drying sublimates ice directly into vapour under vacuum, producing a lightweight product.

questions.text: A dehydrator used in fish processing works by
options: Circulating warm dry air to remove moisture from fish
questions.explanation: Dehydrators remove moisture by blowing warm air over fish, inhibiting microbial growth.

questions.text: The cold chain in fisheries refers to
options: A chain used to tie fish together
Maintaining low temperatures from harvest through processing to the consumer
The temperature of deep ocean water
questions.explanation: The cold chain ensures fish stays chilled throughout the entire post-harvest handling process.

questions.text: Feed pellets used in aquaculture are produced by
options: A feed mill using extrusion or pressing techniques
questions.explanation: Commercial fish feeds are manufactured in mills using precise ingredient formulations.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Sinking feed is used in" by choosing the correct option.
options: Bottom-feeding species like catfish and carp
questions.explanation: Sinking pellets are formulated for species that feed at or near the pond bottom.

questions.text: Vitamin C is essential in fish feeds because it
options: Supports immune function, wound healing and collagen formation
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is critical for immune health, tissue repair and stress resistance in fish.

questions.text: Lipids in fish feeds are important because they
options: Provide concentrated energy and essential fatty acids
questions.explanation: Lipids are energy-dense and supply essential omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids.

questions.text: Moist feed in aquaculture is made by mixing dry ingredients with
options: Water or fresh fish to form a soft, wet mixture
questions.explanation: Moist feeds combine dry meal with water or fresh fish to improve palatability.

questions.text: Natural food organisms in fish ponds include
questions.explanation: Phytoplankton, zooplankton, insect larvae and worms are natural food sources in ponds.

questions.text: Complete the statement: "Plankton in a fish pond consists of" by choosing the correct option.
options: Microscopic organisms that drift with water currents
questions.explanation: Plankton are small organisms that drift in water, including phytoplankton and zooplankton.

questions.text: Supplementary feeding in fish ponds is necessary when
options: Natural food supply is insufficient for the stocking density
questions.explanation: When stocking density exceeds what natural food can support, supplementary feeds are needed.

questions.text: Aeration in aquaculture ponds is most critical during
options: Periods of high stocking density, hot weather and algal bloom crashes
questions.explanation: Oxygen demand peaks in hot weather, dense stocks and when decomposing algae deplete oxygen.

questions.text: Integrated fish farming may combine fish culture with
options: Poultry, livestock or crop production for mutual benefit
questions.explanation: Integrated systems use waste from one enterprise as input for another, improving sustainability.
